questions.question: 밑줄 친 단어의 우리말 뜻으로 가장 적절한 것은?

③ <u>Even</u> my little brother can solve this puzzle. (심지어)

questions.passage:
This is a special market for funny-looking fruits and vegetables. It opens every Saturday morning. ⓐ<u>They</u> greet each other and start to talk.
Apple: What a nice day! ⓑ<u>I</u>'m here because I have many spots on my skin. People think that I'm tasteless. ⓒ<u>They</u> are wrong! My spots are not (A)[ harmful / harmfully ]. I taste great.
Kiwi: I'm round but very small. Farmers don't want to sell ⓓ<u>me</u> (B)[ because / because of ] my size. Who cares about size? ⓔ<u>I</u>'m sweet and delicious.
Carrot: Do you see that ⓕ<u>I</u> have three legs? I look funny because my roots are like a fork. I just tried to avoid stones in the ground and grew three legs. I'm fresh and (C)[ make / makes ] healthy juice.
Apple: I'm glad to see you all! I want to meet more fruits and vegetables like us. Do you know any?
Kiwi: How about eggplants? Some eggplants are bent too much. Supermarkets don't sell ⓖ<u>them</u> because people like straight eggplants.

questions.passage:
Art class was over. Vashti ①<u>did not left</u> the classroom. Her paper was empty.
Vashti's teacher looked at the empty paper.
"Ah! It's a polar bear in a snowstorm," she said.
"Very funny!" said Vashti. "I just can't draw." (A)
Her teacher smiled and shook her head.
"Just make a mark. It will take you somewhere."
Vashti picked up a pen and poked the paper.
"There!"
Her teacher picked up the paper and looked at it carefully. She returned the paper to Vashti and said, "Now sign it."
Vashti thought for a moment.
"Well, maybe I can't draw, but I can sign my name."
Next week, Vashti walked into art class. She was surprised. There was a picture above the teacher's desk. It was her dot in a gold frame!
"Hmm! I can ②<u>make a good dot than that</u>!"
She opened her set of watercolors and started to work. (B)
Vashti painted and painted more ③<u>to create dots</u>. A red dot. A yellow dot. A blue dot. She mixed the blue with the yellow. She could make a green dot! She was very happy with ④<u>itself</u>. (C)
"I made lots of little dots. I guess I can make big ones, too." Vashti used a bigger brush and bigger paper ⑤<u>for make bigger dots</u>.

questions.passage:
A few weeks later, the school art show took place. Vashti's many dots were a big success!
Vashti saw a little boy. He was standing beside her.
"You're a great artist. I want to paint like you," he said.
"I'm sure you can. Trust yourself," said Vashti.
"No, I can't even draw a straight line."
Vashti smiled. She handed the boy a piece of paper.
"Show me."
The boy's pencil shook while he drew a line. The line was not straight.
Vashti looked at it carefully and said,
"Please ... sign it."
